subject: Follow-up: Reliability / SLO comparison + next test plan
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@nimbus.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Reliability / SLO comparison + next test plan

Hi Samir — great to meet today. Quick recap from our discovery and the concrete next steps we agreed on: 

1) What we heard from NimbusAI: P95 latency targets ~200ms for inference, steady-state RPS ~2k/sec with 5x burst, hard requirement for 99.9% uptime during business hours, and the ability to failover across regions without data leakage.

2) Key Redwood differentiators we called out: dedicated capacity option (reserved GPU pools) for predictable throughput, automatic KV/prefix caching to keep p95 tight under load, multi-path failover with graceful degradation (model variant fallback), and explicit error-budgeting + alerting per route.

3) Next technical asks we committed to: 
  - Share a short SLO/uptime comparison doc vs. typical hyperscaler inference endpoints (attached).
  - Propose a focused reliability test plan (48-hour soak + controlled regional failover) and schedule two candidate windows.
  - Confirm your traffic profile (burst characteristics, typical seq lengths, auth pattern).

Attachments: redwood-uptime-SLO-comparison.pdf (summary), proposed-multipath-failover-diagram.png

Proposed test windows (PST):
  - Wed Apr 7, 00:00–48:00 (low production risk window)
  - Tue Apr 13, 18:00–20:00 (short canary + failover exercise)

Ask: can you share your preferred window and the traffic profile (sample load script / qps curve) so our SREs can size the dedicated pool and prepare the canary? Also confirm whether you want our Dedicated Reserved pools or a hosted route with guaranteed throughput for the pilot.

Thanks — Ben

--

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Reliability / SLO comparison + next test plan

Ben — thanks for the summary and the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from our side: 

- We can share a representative traffic trace. Typical steady-state is ~2k qps with 10–20% short bursts that spike to ~8–10k for 30–90s. Sequence lengths vary; 80% short (<128 tokens), 20% longer (up to 1024).
- Our SREs want to understand rate-limiting behavior and how you handle global failover — specifically whether sessions or KV caches get rehydrated and how you avoid double-processing during split-brain.
- Is per-route error budget enforcement possible today (we want to throttle non-critical routes when error budgets are depleted)? Also curious about your global SLA during cross-region failover — do you offer a higher-tier SLA for Dedicated customers?

We prefer the Apr 7 48-hour window if you can support it. Please include an agenda for the first 4 hours of the test (smoke + ramp).

Samir
Principal Engineer, NimbusAI
samir@nimbus.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@nimbus.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Reliability / SLO comparison + next test plan

Samir — great details, thank you. Quick answers inline, and attached the SLO comparison PDF we discussed.

- Bursts: we use a combination of pre-warmed blades for Dedicated pools and elastic burst capacity for hosted routes. For Dedicated customers we can size pre-warm to cover your 10k spikes for short windows; for hosted routes we provide a burst policy that accepts brief overage and returns 429s with exponential backoff guidance if limits are exceeded.

- KV / sessions on failover: our multi-path failover preserves KV caches where possible by attempting warm handoff to a compatible instance with the latest KV snapshot; if a perfect warm handoff isn’t possible, we fall back to a model-variant (quantized) that can serve with minimal rehydration. We design the flow to be idempotent at the application layer to avoid double-processing. See attached diagram (proposed-multipath-failover-diagram.png).

- Per-route error budgets: yes — we expose per-route error-budget meters and a policy engine that can throttle or reroute non-critical routes when budgets cross thresholds. That’s supported today for Dedicated and for customers on our advanced observability add-on.

- SLA tiers: Dedicated Reserved offers a 99.95% uptime SLA with latency targets baked into the commit; hosted has a standard 99.9% for production tiers. For pilots we typically operate with a 99.9% expectation but can discuss a short-term higher SLA (contract amendment) for the evaluation period.

Test agenda (first 4 hours) — Apr 7 start 
  0:00–0:15 — smoke checks, certs & auth verification, connect baseline metrics
  0:15–1:00 — ramp to steady-state 2k qps, confirm p95 for short seq lengths
  1:00–3:00 — controlled burst tests to 8–10k for short windows; measure cache hit rate and p95 impact
  3:00–4:00 — simulate regional failover (region drain + cross-region routing) and observe failover latency and error budget effects

We'll have our SREs (Rishi) run the failover exercise and Marissa will lead test orchestration and metrics collection. Can you confirm who at Nimbus will be monitoring and the preferred Slack channel?

Ben

Attachments: redwood-uptime-SLO-comparison.pdf, proposed-multipath-failover-diagram.png

--
Ben Carter

Looping in next steps and internal owner notes.

Ben / Rishi — we should: 
  - Confirm HubSpot record HS-90321 is updated with the Apr 7 test window and attach the traffic trace once Samir shares.
  - Prep a Dedicated pool sizing doc for the pilot (GPU count, pre-warm strategy, cache sizing) and share with Samir by Thu EOD.
  - Rishi: plan for a canary stage where we hit a canary subset of pods with duplicate traffic to validate idempotency (avoid double-processing). Also prepare a post-run errorsheet (error types, 429/503 rates, rehydration time).

Samir / Priya — thanks again for the slot — we’ll send a calendar invite for Apr 7 and share the runbook + dashboards in advance (Drive link in metadata). If you’d like, we can add a short contract amendment for a temporary higher SLA for the pilot — Ben, please draft pricing for a short-term SLA bump and attach.

Marissa
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
